### 1.  Write everything with \(w=e^{iz}\)

\[
\cos z=\frac{e^{iz}+e^{-iz}}2=\frac{w+w^{-1}}2 ,\qquad 
e^{3iz}=w^{3},\;e^{2iz}=w^{2}.
\]

Hence  

\[
\bigl(w-w^{3}\bigr)\frac{w+w^{-1}}2=4w^{2}-2 .
\]

Multiplying by \(2\) and expanding

\[
(w-w^{3})(w+w^{-1})=8w^{2}-4
\Longrightarrow 1-w^{4}=8w^{2}-4 .
\]

Thus   

\[
w^{4}+8w^{2}-5=0 .
\]

---

### 2.  Solve the quartic

Let \(t=w^{2}\;(t\neq0)\).  Then  

\[
t^{2}+8t-5=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
t=-4\pm\sqrt{21}.
\]

Hence  

\[
w^{2}=-4+\sqrt{21}\qquad\text{or}\qquad w^{2}=-(4+\sqrt{21}).
\]

Since \(-4+\sqrt{21}>0\),

\[
w=\pm a,\qquad a:=\sqrt{-4+\sqrt{21}}\;(0<a<1),
\]

and because \(-(4+\sqrt{21})<0\),

\[
w=\pm i b,\qquad b:=\sqrt{\,4+\sqrt{21}\,}\;(b>1).
\]

Thus the four possible values of \(w=e^{iz}\) are  

\[
w\in\{\,\pm a,\;\pm i b\,\}.
\]

---

### 3.  From \(e^{iz}=w\) to \(z\)

Write \(w=r e^{i\theta}\;(r>0,\;\theta\in\mathbb R)\).  
The complex logarithm gives  

\[
iz=\ln r+i(\theta+2\pi k),\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,
\]
\[
\boxed{\;z=(\theta+2\pi k)-i\ln r\; } .
\]

* For \(w=\pm a\): \(r=a\), \(\theta=0\) (for \(+a\)) or \(\theta=\pi\) (for \(-a\)).  
  Hence  

  \[
  z=2\pi k-i\ln a \quad\text{or}\quad
  z=\pi+2\pi k-i\ln a .
  \]

* For \(w=\pm i b\): \(r=b\), \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}\) (for \(+i b\)) or \(\theta=-\frac{\pi}{2}\) (for \(-i b\)).  
  Hence  

  \[
  z=\frac{\pi}{2}+2\pi k-i\ln b \quad\text{or}\quad
  z=-\frac{\pi}{2}+2\pi k-i\ln b .
  \]

Because \(a=\sqrt{-4+\sqrt{21}}\) and \(b=\sqrt{4+\sqrt{21}}\),

\[
\ln a=\frac12\ln\!\bigl(-4+\sqrt{21}\bigr),\qquad
\ln b=\frac12\ln\!\bigl(4+\sqrt{21}\bigr).
\]

---

### 4.  Solutions in Cartesian form  

Writing \(z=x+iy\) we obtain two families:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&x=n\pi,\qquad 
y=-\frac12\ln\!\bigl(-4+\sqrt{21}\bigr),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z,\\[4pt]
&x=\frac{\pi}{2}+n\pi,\qquad 
y=-\frac12\ln\!\bigl(4+\sqrt{21}\bigr),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z .
\end{aligned}}
\]

Equivalently, using the four separate progressions,

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
z&=2\pi k-i\ln\!\sqrt{-4+\sqrt{21}},\\[2pt]
z&=\pi+2\pi k-i\ln\!\sqrt{-4+\sqrt{21}},\\[2pt]
z&=\frac{\pi}{2}+2\pi k-i\ln\!\sqrt{\,4+\sqrt{21}},\\[2pt]
z&=-\frac{\pi}{2}+2\pi k-i\ln\!\sqrt{\,4+\sqrt{21}},
\qquad k\in\mathbb Z .
\end{aligned}}
\]

These are all the solutions of \((e^{iz}-e^{3iz})\cos z=4e^{2iz}-2\) written in Cartesian form.<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
